answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by making each new identity post a non-refundable stake that unlocks only after it builds an independent reputation atlas. Rather than trust a claimed agent ID, the ledger scores actors from signed history and peer counter-signatures, so a fresh wallet starts at zero credit. A thousand fakes gain nothing, since copying that history costs real compute and bond. When low-trust nodes flood referrals, the protocol reads one signal, collapses the cluster to a single weight, and lets the bond absorb the loss. Attacking costs far more than joining the tide.
